sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers the northern tip of Lyndhurst between the Rutherford boundary and Lake Avenue, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. Rutherford Avenue runs along the top edge on the township line, with only its south side drawn; the ground beyond is Rutherford, shown on the map of Garfield. Park Avenue runs diagonally down the left side and Stuyvesant Avenue curves down through the middle from their meeting point at Rutherford Avenue, enclosing a long triangular block; Livingston Avenue runs down the right edge. Lake Avenue, also lettered 4th Avenue, crosses the lower part of the sheet, and Jay Avenue leaves it southward near the lower left. The triangle between Park and Stuyvesant Avenues holds the main industry on the sheet: the Bollenbach Knitting Mills and a vacant brick building, a garage for 25 cars with auto sales and auto body repair shops, and a small factory making smoking pipes, besides a carpenter shop and scattered dwellings. Stores line Stuyvesant Avenue near Rutherford Avenue and both sides of Lake Avenue around Stuyvesant Avenue, including a drug store, a paint store, a plumbing supplies building of concrete block and a row of small stores south of Lake Avenue. The rest of the sheet is frame dwellings on narrow lots, with a long row of nearly identical two-storey houses on the north side of Lake Avenue. Street widths of 50 and 60 feet and water pipe sizes are noted, block numbers 2, 3, 100 and 101 are printed, and the edges refer to sheets 3, 8 and 11.
notes: Lake Avenue is also lettered 4th Avenue.
Rutherford Avenue is the township line; the north side is marked 'Rutherford, see map of Garfield'.
Bollenbach Knitting Mills in the triangle between Park and Stuyvesant Avenues.
The junction of Park, Stuyvesant and Rutherford Avenues was not used as control: the modern node lies about 38 ft east of where the drawn centrelines meet (the area was rebuilt around Route 3).

50 ft. Northern tip: Rutherford Av (township line, south side only), Park Av, Stuyvesant Av, Livingston Av, Lake Av (4th Av), Jay Av; Bollenbach Knitting Mills. One part. Only 4 junctions usable; Park/Stuyvesant/Rutherford modern node ~38 ft off the drawn meeting point and excluded.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers the business centre of Lyndhurst along Stuyvesant Avenue, from beyond Second Avenue at the top to Tontine Avenue at the bottom, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. The Delaware, Lackawanna and Western main line crosses the sheet diagonally from the upper left, with Lyndhurst Station, a brick passenger station of the D. L. and W. Railway, on its north side east of Stuyvesant Avenue, and a trestle siding serving the coal yard of the Stuyvesant Co. Inc. south of the tracks. Jay Avenue runs along the left edge, Court Avenue and Oriental Place cross the left half, and New York Avenue enters from the right edge north of the railroad; Livingston Avenue runs along the right edge at the top and crosses the lower right corner. Stuyvesant Avenue, lettered 50 feet wide, is lined almost continuously with brick stores and offices between the railroad and Tontine Avenue. Named buildings include the Lyndhurst Trust Co. bank, a drug store, a moving picture theatre on the east side of Stuyvesant Avenue, a garage for 60 cars with a sawtooth skylight roof, a hall and woodworking shop at Tontine Avenue, a bake house, a plumber shop, a motorcycle shed, auto stalls of concrete block and the M. E. Church on Tontine Avenue. North of the railroad a brick apartment house, drawn from plans, faces Livingston Avenue. Elsewhere the sheet shows frame dwellings on narrow lots, especially along Court Avenue and Oriental Place. Block numbers 3, 4, 12, 12A, 88, 89 and 100 are printed, and the margins refer to sheets 2, 4, 8 and 11.
notes: Lyndhurst Station of the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railway (main line) stands east of Stuyvesant Avenue.
Stuyvesant Avenue is lettered 50 ft wide but drawn about 32 ft between the building lines along the stores.
Second Avenue is lettered 50 ft wide west of Stuyvesant Avenue and 70 ft east of it, and is offset where it crosses.
Modern Court Avenue continues east of Stuyvesant Avenue to Livingston Avenue south of the railroad; in 1928 only the coal yard occupies that ground.

Junctions with Livingston Avenue at Second Avenue and with Jay Avenue at Court Avenue were not used as control: both streets are cut by the sheet edge and the detected positions disagreed with the rest by 20 to 60 ft.

50 ft. Business centre on Stuyvesant Av from 2nd Av to Tontine Av; DL&W main line and Lyndhurst Station; Court Av, Oriental Pl, Jay Av, Livingston Av, New York Av. One part. Stuyvesant drawn about 32 ft between building lines; Livingston and Jay cut by the sheet edges.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 covers the centre of Lyndhurst around the crossing of Valley Brook Avenue and Stuyvesant Avenue, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. Tontine Avenue runs along the top edge, Travers Place along the left edge and Pine Street along the right edge; Valley Brook Avenue crosses the sheet just above the middle, and Stuyvesant Avenue runs diagonally down through it. Livingston Avenue runs parallel to the right-hand side and jogs eastward where it crosses Valley Brook Avenue, so its northern and southern segments are offset. The sheet shows the small commercial core of the township: a row of brick stores on the south side of Valley Brook Avenue east of Stuyvesant Avenue, marked as drawn from plans, a drug store and other brick stores on the north-west corner, and a cluster of stores and a brick building on the north-east corner beside the public library. Community buildings include the Reed Memorial United Presbyterian Church and the B.P.O.E. Lodge No. 1505, both in the block between Travers Place and Stuyvesant Avenue north of Valley Brook Avenue. The rest of the sheet is frame dwellings with outbuildings and garages on long narrow lots, more closely built along Travers Place and Livingston Avenue south of Valley Brook Avenue, with house numbers along every frontage and water pipe sizes noted in the streets. Block numbers 13, 24, 74, 75, 76 and 77 are printed in the blocks, and the edges carry references to adjoining sheets 3, 5, 8, 11, 12 and 13.
notes: Livingston Avenue jogs at Valley Brook Avenue: the segment south of it is offset about 160 ft east of the northern segment; OpenStreetMap has two nodes for the junction and both are used as control.
Reed Memorial United Presbyterian Church and B.P.O.E. Lodge No. 1505 stand on the block between Travers Place and Stuyvesant Avenue.
Public library on the north side of Valley Brook Avenue east of Stuyvesant Avenue.
50 ft. Valley Brook Av / Stuyvesant Av; Tontine Av, Travers Pl, Livingston Av (jogs at Valley Brook), Pine St; Reed Memorial Presbyterian Church, public library. One part. Pilot sheet.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 covers the ground east of the Lyndhurst business centre between Tontine Avenue and the blocks south of Valley Brook Avenue, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. Pine Street runs along the left edge, Tontine Avenue along the top, and Valley Brook Avenue crosses the sheet just below the middle; Weart Avenue, Lincoln Avenue, Grant Avenue and Cleveland Avenue run down the sheet, Weart and Grant Avenues being offset where they cross Valley Brook Avenue and Lincoln Avenue ending at it. The block between Pine Street and Weart Avenue north of Valley Brook Avenue is laid out in lots but nearly empty; it holds the Lyndhurst Town Hall, a fireproof building of 1925 with the fire department and police department, and a club house. The large block east of it is occupied by the Leslie Co. foundry and machine shop (diagram from office plans), with a foundry, pattern shop and pattern storage, cast shed, storage building, a machine shop with sawtooth roof and an office, served by a siding. In the upper right corner, beside the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western main line, are the coal bins and cement storage of the Riverside Coal and Supply Co. and the roof cement works of the Myers-Lehman Co. Inc. Frame dwellings and a few stores line Cleveland Avenue. South of Valley Brook Avenue the sheet shows rows of frame dwellings on narrow lots, with a few brick stores, a printing plant and a post office of cinder block construction at the corner of Lincoln Avenue. Block numbers 71 to 74 and 78 to 80 are printed, and the margins refer to sheets 4, 6, 8 and 13.
notes: Weart Avenue north of Valley Brook Avenue is the modern Delafield Avenue; south of Valley Brook Avenue it keeps the name Weart Avenue, offset to the west.
Tontine Avenue east of Pine Street no longer exists as a street; the junctions with Weart and Grant Avenues there have no modern counterpart.
Lyndhurst Town Hall (built 1925, fire and police departments) stands between Pine Street and Weart Avenue north of Valley Brook Avenue.
The Leslie Co. foundry and machine shop, the Riverside Coal and Supply Co. and the Myers-Lehman Co. Inc. roof cement works occupy the blocks north of Valley Brook Avenue.
Pine Street is cut by the left edge of the sheet; its two junctions were hand-picked from the drawn east edge and the lettered widths (32 to 38 ft).

50 ft. Tontine Av to below Valley Brook Av between Pine St and Cleveland Av; Town Hall, Leslie Co. foundry, Myers-Lehman roof cement. Weart Av north of Valley Brook is modern Delafield Avenue. One part; control nearly all on the Valley Brook row (weak).

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 covers the Valley Brook Avenue business street between Cleveland Avenue and Millburn Avenue, with the blocks north to the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad and south beyond Laurel Avenue, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. Cleveland Avenue runs down the left edge, Chase Avenue and Green Avenue cross the sheet, both offset where they cross Valley Brook Avenue, and Millburn Avenue runs down the lower right. Second Street runs between Chase and Green Avenues and continues, offset, east of Green Avenue, where First Street runs parallel to it; Laurel Avenue crosses the lower third. The railroad runs along the top edge, and a siding serves Coopers Lumber Yard, with its lumber shed and lumber piles, at the corner of Cleveland Avenue. Valley Brook Avenue is lined on both sides with one and two storey brick stores, including a paint store, a drug store, a gasoline station of concrete block at Cleveland Avenue, a garage for 12 cars of concrete block, and the Sacred Heart Lyceum near Millburn Avenue. Other buildings named are a private garage of tile and brick on Chase Avenue, a contractors yard and a long concrete block building on Green Avenue, a laundry of concrete construction south of Laurel Avenue, and a building marked fire ruins near Green Avenue. The rest of the sheet is frame dwellings with garages on narrow lots. Block numbers 67 to 71, 81, 82, 83, 84A, 84B and 84C are printed, and the margins refer to sheets 5, 7, 8, 9, 13 and 14.
notes: Coopers Lumber Yard with a railroad siding at the corner of Cleveland Avenue, beside the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad.
Chase Avenue and Green Avenue are offset where they cross Valley Brook Avenue; OpenStreetMap has two nodes for Green Avenue there and both are used as control.
Second Street east of Green Avenue and First Street have no matching modern junctions in the reference data and were not used as control.
Millburn Avenue is spelled with a double l on the sheet; the modern name is Milburn Avenue.
50 ft. Valley Brook Av between Cleveland and Millburn Avs; Chase Av, Green Av (both offset at Valley Brook), 2nd St, 1st St, Laurel Av; Coopers Lumber Yard on DL&W siding. One part.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 covers the centre of Kingsland, the eastern part of the township, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. The Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad crosses the top of the sheet, with the Kingsland railroad station and its stairs where Ridge Road passes under the line. Ridge Road runs down the sheet from the station to New Jersey Avenue; Valley Brook Avenue crosses the middle and bends slightly where it meets Ridge Road, and New Jersey Avenue runs along the bottom. Second Street and First Street come in from the left as far as Ridge Road; east of Ridge Road the northern street is lettered Freeman and runs to Castle Terrace. Harrington Avenue, Castle Terrace (also lettered Castels Terrace) and Warren run from Freeman down to Valley Brook Avenue, and Millburn Avenue runs along the left edge; Clinton Terrace starts south of New Jersey Avenue at the bottom. The commercial buildings are along Ridge Road and Valley Brook Avenue: stores, a bake shop with ovens, a bakery, a drug store, the First National Bank, the Ritz Motion Picture Theatre, and a plumber's shop. Institutions are the Lincoln Public School with a hose company on First Street, and the Sacred Heart Roman Catholic Church and its Sunday school between Valley Brook and New Jersey Avenues. A factory making phonograph parts stands near Warren, and a club house on Harrington Avenue. The rest of the sheet is frame dwellings with garages. Block numbers 66, 84A, 84B, 84C, 130, 131, 132A, 132E and 141 are printed, and the margins refer to sheets 6, 9, 10 and 14.
notes: Kingsland railroad station of the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad at Ridge Road.

The street lettered Freeman east of Ridge Road, and Second Street between Ridge Road and Green Avenue, are both modern Freeman Street; Second Street meets Ridge Road about 40 ft north of Freeman, so that junction was not used as control.
First Street is modern Gutheil Place.
Valley Brook Avenue jogs about 25 ft at Ridge Road; the hand-picked Ridge Road / Valley Brook Avenue point is on the centreline of the eastern part.
Millburn Avenue is spelled with a double l on the sheet; the modern name is Milburn Avenue. Its junctions lie at the left edge of the sheet and were not used.
Castle Terrace is also lettered Castels Terrace.
Valley Brook Avenue and New Jersey Avenue are drawn with faint lot lines only, so their junctions were hand-picked.
50 ft. Kingsland: Ridge Rd, Freeman, Harrington, Castle Ter, Warren, 1st St, Valley Brook Av, New Jersey Av, Millburn Av; DL&W at top. One part; 4 automatic and 4 hand-picked points.

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 covers the north-west part of Lyndhurst between Rutherford Avenue, the township line along the top edge, and the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad yards at the bottom, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. Livingston Avenue curves down the left side and Delafield Avenue, which becomes Weart Avenue south of Second Avenue, runs diagonally through the middle. Lafayette Place continues south of Lake Avenue as Grant Avenue, and Lincoln Place and Jenness Avenue cross the east side. The cross streets are Fifth, Sixth, Lake (also lettered 4th Av.), Third, Second and New York Avenues. Most blocks are lined with frame dwellings and garages on narrow lots, with many large blocks, numbered 90 to 105C, still open behind the street frontages. Jefferson School No. 6 stands at Livingston and Delafield Avenues, and a fire alarm box marks Second Avenue at Grant Avenue. Jersey City water supply pipes run along many of the streets. The lower right is taken by the United Cork Companies works, a large complex of oven, finishing and storage buildings with sheds, and by the J. M. Lehman Co. Inc. chocolate machine factory, both served by sidings from the railroad. The railroad tracks cross the lower left diagonally, with the head of Livingston Avenue and Tontine Avenue beyond them in the corner. The top edge carries the legend "See Map of Garfield" for the ground beyond Rutherford Avenue.
notes: Grant Avenue south of Lake Avenue is today Lafayette Place, which is the name OpenStreetMap gives the whole street.
Delafield Avenue meets Weart Avenue at Second Avenue; Delafield Avenue is a modern name that matches the printed name.

Delafield Avenue and Livingston Avenue are curved on the sheet; the junctions on Delafield Avenue fit 3 to 4 m worse than the rest and Livingston Avenue at New York Avenue, Delafield at 5th and 6th Avenues were left out.
Lincoln Place and Jenness Avenue are not matched to modern nodes and give no control.

100 ft. North: Rutherford Av (township line, south side only) to the DL&W; Livingston, Delafield (Weart Av south of 2nd Av), Lafayette Pl (Grant Av south of Lake = OSM Lafayette Place), Jenness Av, Lincoln Pl; 6th, 5th, Lake (4th), 3rd, 2nd Avs, New York Av; United Cork Companies and J. M. Lehman Co works. One part. Curved Delafield and Livingston junctions 3-4 m off; 5th/Delafield, 6th/Delafield, Livingston/New York excluded. No control east of Lafayette Pl (Jenness, Lincoln Pl have no matching modern nodes); seam with sheet 9 checked on a preview.

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 covers the northern part of Kingsland, the eastern district of Lyndhurst township, from Rutherford Avenue, the township line along the top, down to Milton Avenue and Pennsylvania Avenue beside the railroad at the bottom. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. Ridge Road, Summit Avenue, and Orient Way run down the sheet as long, slightly converging streets, crossed by Sixth, Fifth, Lake (also lettered 4th Av.), Third, Second and New York Avenues. Below New York Avenue Furman Place and Irving Place are short streets running to Milton Avenue, and Mountain Way and Pennsylvania Avenue complete the lower right corner. The blocks, numbered 85 and 92 to 130, are filled mainly with frame dwellings and garages along the street fronts, with deep, narrow lots and a large share of land still vacant, especially around blocks 108, 111 and 112 on the east side. Columbus School No. 5 stands on Lake Avenue between Ridge Road and Summit Avenue, and the Lindy Apartments and a second apartment building are at the upper left. A group of stores and a motion picture house with other buildings stand at Ridge Road and Milton Avenue, and another small commercial group at Ridge Road and Second Avenue. St. Joseph's Catholic Cemetery fills the open lower left, with the scale bar printed within it. The railroad and Main Line tracks cross the bottom edge. The top margin carries the legend "See Map of Garfield" for the ground beyond Rutherford Avenue.
notes: Lake Avenue is also lettered 4th Av. on this sheet.

Furman Place and Irving Place meet New York Avenue at offset corners; the junctions of Furman Place and of Summit Avenue with New York Avenue were rejected as 12 to 14 m off the fit and are not used as control.
Milton Avenue at Summit Avenue and Third Avenue at Ridge Road were also rejected by the fit.

100 ft. Kingsland north: Rutherford Av to Pennsylvania Av; Ridge Rd, Summit Av, Orient Way, Mountain Way, Furman Pl, Irving Pl, Milton Av; 6th to 2nd Avs, New York Av; St. Joseph's Catholic Cemetery. One part. Offset junctions on New York Av and Milton/Summit rejected.

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10 covers the eastern part of Kingsland, from New York Avenue and Evergreen Place at the top down to Magnolia Avenue at the bottom, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. In the upper half the long north-south streets Mountain Way, Orient Way, Newark Avenue, Van Buren, Lafayette Avenue, Madison and Monroe cross Pennsylvania Avenue, which is lettered Furman Av. east of Orient Way, and Smith Av., which continues Valley Brook Av. east of Newark Avenue. The blocks between them, numbered 119 to 138, are long, deep and narrow, with houses mostly along the street fronts and much open ground behind. A diagonal belt of Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad tracks crosses the sheet from the upper left to the lower right, cutting off block 130 and the triangular area around Valley Brook Avenue, where a coal yard and a cement block works stand. Below Valley Brook Avenue the sheet shows the corner of block 141 and the small residential grid of blocks 143 to 145 between New Jersey and Marin Avenues, with First to Fourth Streets running down to Magnolia Avenue, a hotel at Marin Avenue and Newark Avenue, and a Jersey City Water Supply Company 72 inch main along Marin Avenue. At the lower right are the D. L. and W. R. R. car shops, with locomotive, transfer table, paint and passenger shops, and above them the New Jersey Brick Co. works with its kilns and storage shed. The scale bar is printed in block 148.
notes: Furman Av., east of Orient Way, is today part of Pennsylvania Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Smith Av. is today part of Valley Brook Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Madison Street at Pennsylvania Avenue was rejected by the fit at 8 m and is not used as control.

The drawn 4th, 3rd, 2nd and 1st Streets in the lower left are modern 4th Street, 3rd Street, Lewandowski Street and Orient Way; through this sheet's fit their junctions with New Jersey and Marin Avenues come out 7 to 11 m from the modern nodes and the detector paired the wrong lines there, so they are not used as control.

100 ft. East Kingsland: New York Av, Evergreen Pl, Pennsylvania Av, Furman Av (= OSM Pennsylvania Avenue east of Orient Way), Smith Av (= OSM Valley Brook Avenue), Valley Brook, New Jersey, Marin, Magnolia Avs; Orient Way, Newark Av, Van Buren, Lafayette, Madison, Monroe, Warren, Nelson; DL&W car shops, New Jersey Brick Co. One part. Lower-left 4th, 3rd, 2nd (= Lewandowski Street) and 1st Sts (= Orient Way): tried as control by the lead, the detector paired wrong lines (3-11 m), left out.

sheet-11-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 11 is the main map: the north-west corner of Lyndhurst township along the Passaic River, from the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad and Lake Av. (4th Av.) at the top right down to Valley Brook Avenue and beyond at the bottom, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. It is bounded at the upper left by a heavy line that separates it from part 2, an inset of the ground between Lake and Rutherford Avenues drawn over the river. Riverside Avenue follows the river shore on the left. Between Court Avenue and Tontine Avenue, Riverside, Peabody, Park, Webster and Jay Avenues run in converging diagonals through blocks 6 to 11, which are largely open, with scattered frame dwellings, an auto repair shop, a filling station and a pond in block 6; Oriental Place leaves Jay Avenue on the right. The railroad double track crosses the top right. South of Tontine Avenue the plan changes to a regular grid of Watson, Lyndhurst and Willow Avenues and Travers Place, running down to Valley Brook Avenue and beyond, with blocks 14 to 23 closely built with frame dwellings and stores. St. Matthews Evangelical Lutheran Church stands at Willow Avenue and Travers Place and the Masonic Club at the bottom. A triangular block 18 lies between Riverside Avenue and Watson Avenue, with an auto repair shop at its point. A compass rose and the scale bar are printed over the open ground by the river at the lower left.
notes: The heavy line at the upper left is not a boundary on the ground: the area beyond it (part 2) lies about 450 m to the east, between Lake and Rutherford Avenues, and is drawn over the river at the same scale and rotation.
Court Avenue at Peabody Avenue was rejected by the fit at 16 m; Court Avenue / Park Avenue and Court Avenue / Webster Avenue are two modern nodes for one drawn junction and both are used.
Riverside Avenue and Peabody Avenue are used only where they meet Tontine Avenue.

100 ft. North-west along the Passaic River. TWO parts. Part 1 (main): Riverside, Peabody, Park, Webster, Jay Avs from Court Av to Tontine Av, then Watson, Lyndhurst, Willow Avs, Travers Pl to Valley Brook Av. Part 2 (upper left, beyond the heavy line): inset of the ground between Lake Av (4th Av) and Rutherford Av west of Park Av (Riverside, Kearney Avs), drawn at the same scale and rotation but over the river, about 450 m west of its true place; placed from 3 hand-picked junctions and 1 detected (low confidence).

sheet-11-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 11 is the upper left corner of the sheet, cut off by a heavy line: an inset of the ground between Lake Av. (4th Av.) and Rutherford Avenue, the township line with Rutherford, west of Park Avenue, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and at the same rotation as the main part but placed over the river, about 450 m west of where it lies. Riverside Avenue runs along the Passaic River on the left, Kearney Avenue through the middle and Park Avenue along the heavy line on the right; Lake Avenue crosses the bottom. Kearney Avenue is lettered "Not Opened" and "Impassable Dec. 1927". The ground is laid out in long lots in blocks 1 and 1A and is mostly open, with a few frame dwellings along Riverside Avenue and at the top along Rutherford Avenue, an auto repair shop near Lake Avenue and three dwellings facing Lake Avenue. A steel draw bridge over the river is noted at the top left corner, and the legend "Rutherford - See Map of Garfield" is printed above Rutherford Avenue, whose north side is not drawn. A 6 inch water pipe runs along Riverside Avenue, Park Avenue and Lake Avenue.
notes: Placed from three hand-picked junctions (Park and Riverside Avenues at Rutherford Avenue, Park Avenue at Lake Avenue) and the detected Kearney Street / Lake Avenue junction; low confidence.
Kearney Avenue as lettered is today Kearney Street; its modern junction with Lake Avenue fits 9 m off, probably because the street was not yet opened on its later line.
The inset is drawn about 450 m west of its true position, over the river; it was split from the main part for that reason.

100 ft. North-west along the Passaic River. TWO parts. Part 1 (main): Riverside, Peabody, Park, Webster, Jay Avs from Court Av to Tontine Av, then Watson, Lyndhurst, Willow Avs, Travers Pl to Valley Brook Av. Part 2 (upper left, beyond the heavy line): inset of the ground between Lake Av (4th Av) and Rutherford Av west of Park Av (Riverside, Kearney Avs), drawn at the same scale and rotation but over the river, about 450 m west of its true place; placed from 3 hand-picked junctions and 1 detected (low confidence).

sheet-12.description: Sheet 12 covers the south-west part of Lyndhurst from the lower ends of Watson, Lyndhurst and Willow Avenues in the north to Copeland Avenue in the south, and from Riverside Avenue and the Passaic River on the left to Stuyvesant Avenue and Prospect Place on the right. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. The east-west streets are Fern, Post, Forest, Page, Kingsland and Copeland Avenues, crossed by short side streets named Alder, Ash, Beach, Cypress, Elm, Fir and Hazel in blocks 25C and 25D. The blocks, numbered 19 to 29 and 35, are filled with close rows of frame dwellings with garages, except blocks 26, 27 and 27A, where houses stand only along the street fronts and large areas behind them are open. Between Fern and Post Avenues a broad strip lettered Jersey City Water Supply Co. Right of Way crosses the sheet in block 25A and 25B, carrying 72 inch pipes. A school, River Road School, and a woodworking shop and a contractor's yard stand beside Riverside Avenue, and Mt. Carmel R. C. Church is on Kingsland Avenue. At the lower left Riverside Avenue curves down to Kingsland Avenue, where a fire alarm box, a filling station, a service station, a cement stone works and a steel draw bridge across the Passaic River are drawn on block 35. The scale bar and compass are printed in block 27.
notes: The street lettered Cypress south of Fern Avenue is the same line as modern Willow Avenue; OpenStreetMap has no Cypress Avenue here.
Fir, the side street between Elm and Hazel, is Oak Street in OpenStreetMap; Beach is Beech Street.

Stuyvesant Avenue is lettered along the right edge at the top and Prospect Place along it below Forest Avenue; modern Stuyvesant Avenue runs close to the Prospect Place line, which was matched to OpenStreetMap Prospect Place.
The jogs of Willow Avenue at Forest, Page and Kingsland Avenues were excluded from the control; Fern Avenue and Willow Avenue is used, Post Avenue and Willow Avenue was rejected by the fit at 9.5 m.
Elm Street at Forest Avenue was rejected by the fit at 6.4 m.

100 ft. South-west: Riverside Av to Prospect Pl, Fern to Copeland Avs; Watson, Lyndhurst, Willow Avs, Travers Pl, Post, Forest, Page, Kingsland Avs; Alder, Ash, Beach (= OSM Beech Street), Cypress (= OSM Willow Avenue south of Fern), Elm, Fir (= OSM Oak Street), Hazel; Jersey City Water Supply Co right of way. One part. Willow jogs at Page/Kingsland/Forest excluded.

sheet-13.description: Sheet 13 covers the central residential district of Lyndhurst between Stuyvesant Avenue and Chase Avenue, from Fern Avenue in the north to Copeland Avenue and Park Place in the south, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. Stuyvesant Avenue runs diagonally down the left of the sheet, with Prospect Place and the end of Hazel Avenue beyond it; Livingston Avenue and Lincoln Avenue end at Fern Avenue, and Weart Avenue, continued south of Page Avenue as Twelfth Street, crosses the middle. Grant Avenue runs from Fern Avenue to Forest Avenue, Paul Place is a short lane off Forest Avenue, and Chase Avenue, lettered Chase Avenue (9th Street) south of Page Avenue, where it is offset, runs down the right side with Tenth Street, Van Eyck Court and Eighth Street. The right of way of the Jersey City Water Supply Company, carrying two 72 inch water pipes, crosses the sheet between Fern and Post Avenues. Public buildings are Franklin School at Stuyvesant and Fern Avenues, Lyndhurst High School with its auditorium and gymnasium on Weart Avenue, Roosevelt Public School between Stuyvesant Avenue and Twelfth Street, and St. Thomas Episcopal Church on Stuyvesant Avenue near Forest Avenue. The rest is frame dwellings with garages on narrow lots, densest along Forest and Page Avenues, with a few brick stores on Stuyvesant and Kingsland Avenues and around Chase Avenue; the large blocks 58A, 62 and 64 are still largely open. Blocks 25B, 25D, 26A, 27, 29, 55 to 59B, 61A, 62 to 64B and 71 to 75 are numbered, and the margins refer to sheets 4, 5, 12, 14, 16 and 17.
notes: 12th Street between Page Avenue and Kingsland Avenue is today part of Weart Avenue.
Chase Avenue south of Page Avenue is lettered Chase Avenue (9th Street) and is offset from Chase Avenue north of Page Avenue; both junctions with Page Avenue are used as control.
Eighth Street is offset at Kingsland Avenue; OpenStreetMap has both nodes and both are used as control.
Hazel Avenue is today Hazel Street.
Lyndhurst High School, Franklin School, Roosevelt Public School and St. Thomas Episcopal Church are on the sheet.
Modern Maple Avenue crosses block 58A between Weart Avenue and 10th Street; it is not drawn in 1928.
100 ft. Stuyvesant Av to Chase Av, Fern Av to Copeland Av; Post, Forest, Page, Kingsland Avs, Weart, Grant. One part; configured by the first lead.

sheet-14.description: Sheet 14 covers the south-eastern part of the Kingsland district of Lyndhurst, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. The sheet is a block of regular streets cut diagonally by Ridge Road, lettered 80 ft wide, which runs from New Jersey Avenue at the top to Kingsland Avenue and Park Place at the bottom. West of Ridge Road the parallel streets are Fern, Post, Forest, Page and Kingsland Avenues, crossed by Chase, Green and Millburn Avenues, Rudolph Place, Octavia Place and the numbered streets 8th, 7th and 6th, with Park Place along the foot. Frame dwellings with garages stand close together along Post, Forest, Page and Kingsland Avenues, and many blocks in the middle and lower left are still open lots. The Jersey City Water Supply Company right of way crosses the upper left between Fern and Post Avenues. East of Ridge Road, Marin, Magnolia, Brisbin and Baldwin Avenues and Clinton Terrace and 4th Street are laid out as large numbered blocks (142, 151 to 154, 162, 163) that are almost empty, apart from Clinton Apartments on Clinton Terrace, the Westminster Presbyterian Church and a contractor's yard near Ridge Road, and St. Michael's Polish R.C. Church with its rectory and the Polish School and Club near Baldwin Avenue. A garage and new lots occupy the lower right corner along 4th Street. The compass, the Lyndhurst oval stamp and the scale bar are printed on the sheet, and the margins refer to sheets 6, 7, 10, 13, 15, 16 and 17.
notes: Millburn Avenue as lettered is today Milburn Avenue.
Brisbin Avenue is today Brisbin Street.
Ridge Road is lettered 80 ft wide; its detected junctions are 1 to 3 m off, but the pair of lines measured is about 50 ft apart.
Chase Avenue at the left edge and the streets beyond it belong to sheet 13; its junctions with Post, Forest and Page are boundary points and Chase / Page was left out as 5 m off.
Sixth Street and 7th Street south of Kingsland Avenue, and 8th Street, are offset from their northern parts; the modern nodes on both sides are used.

100 ft. Chase Av to 4th St / east of Ridge Rd, New Jersey Av to Park Pl; Marin, Magnolia, Brisbin, Fern, Post, Forest, Page, Baldwin, Kingsland Avs; Green, Millburn (= OSM Milburn Avenue), Octavia Pl, Rudolph Pl, Clinton Ter, 4th-8th Sts. One part. Ridge Rd drawn about 50 ft between edges against 80 ft parcels (narrow flags, residuals fine). Chase Av boundary points (Post, Forest, Page) excluded: 3.5-4.7 m off sheet 13's interior measurement.

sheet-15.description: Sheet 15 covers the south-eastern corner of the Kingsland district at the Newark and Union Avenue edge of the township, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. The upper right is occupied by the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad car shops, shown as a group of large pink buildings (the Passenger Shop, Mill Building, Finished Lumber, Varnish Room, Wash Room, Power House, Dry Kiln and Carpenter Shop), a transfer table and a fan of tracks, with the note that admittance is refused and the plan is taken from diagrams. Left of the shops, the streets from Magnolia Avenue to Kingsland Avenue (Brisbin Avenue, Page Avenue, Bloomfield Place and the numbered streets 3rd, 2nd and 1st) enclose blocks 147 to 161 of which only the rows along Page Avenue and Bloomfield Place are built. South of Kingsland Avenue, Ten Eyck Avenue, Olive and the same numbered streets cross a large area of long narrow lots (blocks 165 to 172) that are mostly unbuilt, with houses grouped along Ten Eyck Avenue and Newark Avenue. Newark Avenue runs diagonally from Kingsland Avenue to the bottom right, where Union Avenue, lettered Union Av. (Jauncy Av.) and carrying the Lyndhurst and North Arlington township line, runs across the foot of the sheet. Swayne Avenue and Ewing Avenue are laid out in North Arlington at the lower right. The sheet adjoins sheets 14 and 17, and the margins also refer to sheet 10.
notes: The 2nd Street of 1928 is today Lewandowski Street; 3rd Street and 1st Street south of Kingsland Avenue keep their names.
The 1st Street north of Kingsland Avenue, lettered 1st St, is today Orient Way.
Newark Avenue south of Kingsland Avenue is today Schuyler Avenue.
Brisbin Avenue is today Brisbin Street.
Union Avenue is lettered with Jauncy Avenue in brackets, the spelling printed on sheets 15 to 17; the township line runs along it.
Olive and 1st Street at Ten Eyck Avenue are not drawn on a line the modern nodes follow; those junctions were left out.
The car shops are not part of the street plan and give no control.

100 ft. South-east: Magnolia Av to Union Av (Jauncy Av, township line with North Arlington); Brisbin, Page, Kingsland, Ten Eyck, Newark Avs (Newark south of Kingsland = OSM Schuyler Avenue), Bloomfield Pl, 3rd, 2nd (= OSM Lewandowski Street), 1st Sts (north of Kingsland = OSM Orient Way), Olive, Swayne, Ewing Avs; DL&W car shops. One part; control thin on the shops side.

sheet-16.description: Sheet 16 covers the southern part of Lyndhurst between Stuyvesant Avenue on the left and the Chase Avenue and Washington Street area on the right, from Copeland Avenue and Park Place at the top to Jauncy Avenue at the bottom, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. The sheet is a regular grid. Stuyvesant Avenue runs down the left edge and Chase Avenue, lettered with 9th Street, down the middle right, with Tyler, Lincoln, Monroe, Madison and Jefferson Streets between them, 10th, 8th and 7th Streets and Washington, Adams and Cedar further right, and Copeland, Sanford, Thomas, Naples, Summer, Wilson, Harding and Roosevelt Avenues crossing them. Dwellings stand along Stuyvesant Avenue, along Park Place and Summer Avenue at the top right and along Wilson, Harding and Roosevelt Avenues at the right; the large middle blocks (36, 43 to 47A) are nearly empty and several of the streets between them are marked not opened. In the lower left, Riverside Avenue runs diagonally from Stuyvesant Avenue towards Jauncy Avenue, and the lower half is largely open ground (block 202 and the blocks 35D and 36) with a few scattered buildings, and the township line marked North Arlington along Jauncy Avenue. The compass is at the lower left, and the margins refer to sheets 13, 14 and 17.
notes: Tyler, Lincoln and Monroe are today Tyler Street, Lincoln Street and Monroe Street; Madison, Jefferson and Adams have no modern node on this line.
Chase Avenue (9th Street) is offset from Chase Avenue north of Summer Avenue; its modern nodes are used.
Naples is not in modern OpenStreetMap.
Monroe Street, Riverside Avenue and Jauncy Avenue junctions in the lower left were not detected.
Stuyvesant Avenue is drawn only about 26 ft between edges against 49 ft in parcels.

100 ft. South: Copeland Av to Jauncy Av, Stuyvesant Av to Chase Av (9th St); Sanford, Thomas, Summer, Wilson, Harding, Roosevelt Avs, Naples; Tyler, Lincoln, Monroe, Madison, Jefferson, Washington, Adams; Riverside Av. One part. Stuyvesant drawn about 26 ft between edges against 49 ft parcels.

sheet-17-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 17 is the main map of the sheet, the area south of the heavy line that runs from the left edge across to the lower right. It is the south-eastern part of Lyndhurst on the North Arlington border, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. A regular grid of streets fills the left and middle: Park Place, Summer Avenue, Thomas Avenue, Wilson, Harding and Roosevelt Avenues cross the numbered streets 7th, 6th and 5th, with Jauncy Avenue along the foot of the sheet. Dwellings fill the rows along Park Place, Summer Avenue and most of 6th and 5th Streets, with blocks 36B, 37, 38, 39 and 52 to the left and 215 to 217 beyond. Ridge Road runs near-vertically through the middle, lettered 80 ft wide in places, with the Washington School and the Liva Bros. cast stone works near it. Ten Eyck Avenue, 4th Street and 3rd Street divide the long lots of blocks 163, 164, 168 and 169 on the right; the heavy line on the upper right marks the edge of the area beyond. Union Avenue, lettered Union Av. (Jauncy Av.) with the North Arlington township line, crosses the lower right, below which Millar Place and 4th Street serve a block of newly built houses (218, 205). The compass belongs to part 2. Margins refer to sheets 14, 15 and 16.
notes: Jauncy Avenue is the spelling printed; modern OpenStreetMap has Jauncey Avenue and Union Avenue.
The heavy line is the limit of this part; the area above it is part 2 and falls elsewhere on the ground, at the same rotation.
Swamp is noted beyond the heavy line at the upper right.
Park Place and Ridge Road junctions along the heavy line are measured from the drawn edges and agree to 0.3 m.
7th Street / Jauncy Avenue was not detected.

100 ft. TWO parts split at the heavy line. Part 1 (main, below): Park Pl to Union Av (Jauncy Av), 7th to 3rd Sts, Ridge Rd, Summer, Thomas, Wilson, Harding, Roosevelt, Ten Eyck Avs. Part 2 (above): Copeland, Sanford, Riverside, Meyer, Thomas Avs, Wiedemann Pl (= OSM Weidermann Place), Cedar, Paul, Stuyvesant, Naples, along the Passaic River; drawn at the same rotation but several hundred metres north-west of part 1 on the ground.

sheet-17-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 17 is the north-western section of the sheet above the heavy line, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. It shows the district of Lyndhurst along the Passaic River between Copeland Avenue at the top and Naples Street at the bottom, an area that is not contiguous with part 1 on the ground although it is printed on the same sheet at the same rotation. Along the top, Copeland Avenue and Sanford Avenue run across a strip of narrow lots with scattered frame dwellings, with Stuyvesant Avenue at the right edge and a blank block 30 between them. Riverside Avenue, a wide street running diagonally from upper left to lower right through blocks 31 and 35, is bordered by a few dwellings; the heavy line follows its lower edge. East of it, Wiedemann Place, Cedar, Paul, Meyer Avenue and Thomas Avenue enclose blocks 32, 32A, 33, 34 and 36A, with a line of small houses along each. In the upper left corner the Passaic River is shown in blue running down to the sheet's compass, with an auto wrecking yard on the bank (block 35). Naples runs across the foot of the right side, with a building marked fire ruins. The Lyndhurst oval stamp and the sheet numbers 12, 13 and 16 appear in the margins.
notes: The part is placed from junctions of Sanford, Paul, Meyer and Thomas Avenues with Stuyvesant Avenue, Cedar, Wiedemann Place and Meyer Avenue; modern OpenStreetMap spells Weidermann Place.
Riverside Avenue / Stuyvesant Avenue near the heavy line was left out as 4.5 m off.
Part 2 is drawn at the same rotation as part 1 but lies several hundred metres to the north-west of it on the ground; the two areas are joined along the heavy line on the printed sheet.
Naples is not in modern OpenStreetMap.

100 ft. TWO parts split at the heavy line. Part 1 (main, below): Park Pl to Union Av (Jauncy Av), 7th to 3rd Sts, Ridge Rd, Summer, Thomas, Wilson, Harding, Roosevelt, Ten Eyck Avs. Part 2 (above): Copeland, Sanford, Riverside, Meyer, Thomas Avs, Wiedemann Pl (= OSM Weidermann Place), Cedar, Paul, Stuyvesant, Naples, along the Passaic River; drawn at the same rotation but several hundred metres north-west of part 1 on the ground.
